feature: Add AI Difficulty Selector (Easy / Medium / Hard)

current_state.game_mode: 2-player only — no AI or single-player support exists in game.js
current_state.ai_logic: None — game.js has zero minimax, random-move, or difficulty logic
current_state.ui_components: turn-indicator, 3x3 board grid, status-message, controls (New Game / Reset Score), scoreboard
current_state.module_exports: WIN_LINES, checkWinner, checkDraw, switchPlayer, checkWin, init, startNewGame, resetScore, handleMove, _getState, _setState
current_state.test_infrastructure: Jest (jsdom) + Playwright; 12 test files covering logic, DOM, E2E, accessibility, CSS animations

key_constraints: Human always plays X; AI always plays O in single-player mode
Easy: 100% random empty cell selection (fully beatable)
Medium: 40% minimax / 60% random (beatable with consistent play)
Hard: full minimax + alpha-beta pruning — provably unbeatable (optimal play = draw)
Difficulty selector must be HIDDEN when 2-player mode is active; VISIBLE only in single-player mode
All neon styling must use existing CSS custom properties — no new color values except Easy green (#00ff88)
AI move must be scheduled asynchronously (300ms setTimeout) so human move renders before AI responds
Board must be interactively locked (pointer-events + JS guard) during AI thinking window
Pending AI timeout must be cancelled in startNewGame() and setGameMode() to prevent stale callbacks
minimax must NOT permanently mutate the passed boardState (must backtrack after every branch)
All existing 2-player tests must continue to pass without modification
No third-party libraries — pure vanilla JS
analysis.dom_order_dependency: The CSS general sibling combinator (.turn-indicator.is-x ~ .board) remains valid when new elements are inserted between turn-indicator and board because ~ matches ANY subsequent sibling, not only the immediately adjacent one.

minimax_design.scoring: O wins: +10 - depth (prefer faster wins); X wins: depth - 10 (negative, prefer slower losses); draw: 0
minimax_design.pruning: Standard alpha-beta: alpha starts -Infinity, beta starts +Infinity; prune when beta <= alpha

difficulty_tiers.easy: 100% random empty cell — Math.random() selects uniformly from getEmptyCells()
difficulty_tiers.medium: Math.random() < 0.4 uses getBestMove() (optimal); else uses randomMove() — 40% optimal / 60% random
difficulty_tiers.hard: Always getBestMove() via full minimax + alpha-beta — never loses

implementation_plan.description: Verify current branch is feature/ai-difficulty-selector (git branch --show-current). Confirm game.js and index.html are in baseline 2-player state.
Add new module-level state variables to game.js after existing state block: gameMode ('2player'), aiDifficulty ('medium'), aiThinking (false), isAIMove (false), aiTimeoutId (null).
Add new DOM reference variables in the DOM Helpers section of game.js: modeSelector, difficultySelector, labelX, labelO.

Implement five pure AI helper functions in a new AI Logic section in game.js: (a) getEmptyCells(boardState) returns array of null indices; (b) randomMove(boardState) returns a random index from getEmptyCells(); (c) minimax(boardState, isMaximizing, depth, alpha, beta) with alpha-beta pruning and backtracking — O wins: +10-depth, X wins: depth-10, draw: 0; (d) getBestMove(boardState) iterates empty cells calling minimax on spread copies, returns highest-scoring index; (e) getAIMove(boardState, difficulty) dispatches to easy/medium/hard logic.
Add lockBoard() (adds 'board--locked' class to #board) and unlockBoard() (removes it) DOM helpers to game.js. These work with CSS rule: .board--locked .cell { pointer-events: none; cursor: default; }

Add scheduleAIMove() — sets aiThinking=true, calls lockBoard(), stores setTimeout(handleAIMove, 300) in aiTimeoutId. Add handleAIMove() — clears aiTimeoutId, exits if gameOver, calls getAIMove([...board], aiDifficulty), if move !== -1 sets isAIMove=true, calls handleMove(move), resets isAIMove; unconditionally sets aiThinking=false and calls unlockBoard().

Modify handleMove() in game.js: (a) add guard 'if (aiThinking && !isAIMove) return' immediately after existing first guard; (b) at end of function after updateScoreCardHighlight(), add AI trigger: 'if (gameMode === "1player" && !gameOver && currentPlayer === "O") { scheduleAIMove(); }'
Modify startNewGame() in game.js — prepend: cancel pending AI timeout (clearTimeout(aiTimeoutId), set to null), reset aiThinking=false, isAIMove=false, call unlockBoard().

Add setGameMode(mode) to game.js: updates gameMode, toggles .active class and aria-pressed on mode buttons, shows/hides difficultySelector via .hidden class, updates score labels (Player X/Player O <-> You/CPU), cancels any pending AI timeout, calls startNewGame().
Add setDifficulty(difficulty) to game.js: updates aiDifficulty, removes .active from all .diff-btn elements, adds .active to the matching button.

Modify init() in game.js: cache modeSelector, difficultySelector, labelX, labelO DOM references; bind click listeners to all .mode-btn elements (call setGameMode(btn.dataset.mode)); bind click listeners to all .diff-btn elements (call setDifficulty(btn.dataset.difficulty)).

Update module.exports in game.js: add getEmptyCells, randomMove, minimax, getBestMove, getAIMove, lockBoard, unlockBoard, scheduleAIMove, setGameMode, setDifficulty, _getAIState (() => ({ gameMode, aiDifficulty, aiThinking, isAIMove })). Update _setState to also accept gameMode, aiDifficulty, aiThinking, isAIMove fields.

Add CSS in index.html <style> block before responsive tweaks section: .mode-selector and .difficulty-selector (pill container — flex row, bg-surface, color-border, border-radius 999px, padding 4px); .mode-btn and .diff-btn (transparent background, color-muted, rounded, transitions); .mode-btn.active (color-x, outline 1px solid color-x, neon glow); .diff-btn.active[data-difficulty='easy'] (#00ff88 green neon); .diff-btn.active[data-difficulty='medium'] (color-o magenta neon); .diff-btn.active[data-difficulty='hard'] (color-x cyan neon); .difficulty-selector.hidden { display: none }; add mode-btn and diff-btn to prefers-reduced-motion transition block.

Add HTML to index.html between #turnIndicator and #board: mode-selector div (role='group', aria-label='Game mode') with two mode-btn buttons (2player active by default); difficulty-selector div (role='group', aria-label='AI difficulty', class includes 'hidden') with three diff-btn buttons (medium active by default). All buttons have type='button' and aria-pressed attributes.

Update GAME_HTML fixture in __tests__/game.dom.test.js to include new mode-selector and difficulty-selector HTML elements so init() can cache those DOM references without null errors. No changes to existing test cases.
Write __tests__/ai.logic.test.js: pure unit tests for getEmptyCells, randomMove, minimax, getBestMove, getAIMove using Jest with node environment (no DOM). See test_plan for full case list.

Write __tests__/ai.dom.test.js: DOM integration tests for mode selector UI, difficulty selector visibility, AI auto-move behavior (jest.useFakeTimers), board locking, startNewGame cancellation, score label switching, and 2-player regression guard. See test_plan for full case list.

new_files.purpose: Pure unit tests for all new AI logic functions using Jest node environment (no DOM). Covers: getEmptyCells correctness on empty/full/partial boards; randomMove validity (only empty cells, valid index range); minimax terminal state scoring (O-win, X-win, draw); minimax depth preference for faster wins; alpha-beta pruning result parity; getBestMove optimal blocking and winning moves; getBestMove center preference on empty board; board immutability invariant; getAIMove difficulty dispatch and statistical distribution tests.

DOM integration tests for mode selector UI and single-player game flow using Jest + jsdom. Covers: mode button active state and aria-pressed accuracy; difficulty selector show/hide toggling; difficulty button active states; score label switching (You/CPU vs Player X/O); AI auto-move after human click using jest.useFakeTimers; AI plays on empty cell; board locking during AI thinking; board unlocking after AI move; startNewGame cancels pending timeout; rapid-click guard; 2-player regression; full game cycle in single-player mode.

rollback_plan: All changes are confined to feature/ai-difficulty-selector branch, isolated from main. Rollback options: (1) Discard uncommitted changes: git restore index.html game.js __tests__/game.dom.test.js && git clean -fd __tests__/ai.logic.test.js __tests__/ai.dom.test.js. (2) Per-commit revert: git revert <commit-hash> creates a new undo commit while preserving history. (3) Branch reset: git reset --hard <last-good-sha> identified via git log --oneline. (4) Full branch deletion: git branch -D feature/ai-difficulty-selector then recreate from main. (5) Post-merge (worst case): git revert -m 1 <merge-commit-sha>. Risk is narrow — only 2 existing files modified, 2 new test files added, zero dependency or CI changes.

risk_assessment.risk: Stale AI setTimeout fires after New Game, placing O on wrong cell
risk_assessment.mitigation: aiTimeoutId stored at module level; startNewGame() always calls clearTimeout(aiTimeoutId) before resetting. handleAIMove() also checks !gameOver as final guard.

risk_assessment.risk: Rapid human clicks during 300ms AI delay cause double-move
risk_assessment.mitigation: Dual-layer: (a) CSS .board--locked .cell { pointer-events: none } blocks mouse clicks; (b) JS guard if (aiThinking && !isAIMove) return blocks keyboard events.

risk_assessment.risk: AI timeout fires after mode switched to 2-player, injecting O into 2-player game
risk_assessment.mitigation: setGameMode() calls clearTimeout(aiTimeoutId) before startNewGame(), cancelling any pending AI callback.

risk_assessment.risk: minimax() permanently mutating shared board module variable
risk_assessment.mitigation: getBestMove() always passes [...board] (spread copy); minimax() backtracks boardState[i] = null after every recursive call. Covered by board immutability test.

risk_assessment.risk: CSS sibling combinator breaking after inserting new elements between turn-indicator and board
risk_assessment.mitigation: General sibling combinator (~) matches any subsequent sibling, not only immediately adjacent. No CSS breakage occurs.

risk_assessment.risk: Existing tests failing because init() looks up #modeSelector/#difficultySelector not in old GAME_HTML fixtures
risk_assessment.mitigation: Step 15 updates GAME_HTML in game.dom.test.js. init() uses null-safe guards (if (el) ...) for new element event binding.
